26 The warning signal on an ambulance has a frequency of 600 Hz. The speed of sound is 330 m s–1.
The ambulance is travelling with a constant velocity of 25 m s–1 towards an observer.
initial position
of ambulance
final position
of ambulance
observer
Which overall change in observed frequency takes place between the times at which the
ambulance is a long way behind the observer and when it is a long way in front of the observer?
A
49 Hz
B
84 Hz
C
91 Hz
D
98 Hz

hints: Notice the diagram: far to the left the $25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ ambulance is moving towards the observer, and far to the right it is moving away from the observer.
Recall the Doppler shift for sound: use $f' = f_0v/(v-v_s)$ when approaching and $f' = f_0v/(v+v_s)$ when receding, with $v=330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate both observed frequencies from $600 \text{ Hz}$ and then subtract the lower receding value from the higher approaching value to get the overall drop.
walkthrough: Identify the two limiting cases: a long way behind means the source is approaching head-on, and a long way in front means the source is receding head-on at $v_s = 25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the Doppler rule for a moving source and stationary observer: approaching shortens the wavelength so $f_{approach} = f_0 v/(v-v_s)$, while receding lengthens it so $f_{recede} = f_0 v/(v+v_s)$.
Substitute $f_0 = 600 \text{ Hz}$ and $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $f_{approach} = 600 \times 330/(330-25) = 600 \times 330/305 \approx 649.2 \text{ Hz}$.
Substitute for the receding case: $f_{recede} = 600 \times 330/(330+25) = 600 \times 330/355 \approx 557.7 \text{ Hz}$.
Find the overall change as the ambulance passes: $\Delta f = f_{approach} - f_{recede} \approx 649.2 - 557.7 \approx 91.5 \text{ Hz}$, a decrease of about $91 \text{ Hz}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: About $49 \text{ Hz}$ is close to only the increase above $600 \text{ Hz}$ when approaching, not the total change from approaching to receding.

B.explanation: About $84 \text{ Hz}$ does not match $f_0v/(v-v_s)-f_0v/(v+v_s)$ with $f_0=600 \text{ Hz}$, $v=330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s=25 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: The difference between $600 \times 330/305 \approx 649 \text{ Hz}$ approaching and $600 \times 330/355 \approx 558 \text{ Hz}$ receding is about $91 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: About $98 \text{ Hz}$ is too large and is not obtained from the approaching frequency minus the receding frequency.
